extra.message: User-controlled post_id is concatenated directly into the SQL query string passed to conn.execute('SELECT * FROM posts WHERE id = ' + post_id). The preceding regex filter (re.match with re.M) is insufficient and bypassable, allowing SQL injection. Use parameterized queries as in the safe get_post() above.

The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as 'qwerty12345'. A known/weak secret key enables session cookie forgery and flash-message tampering. Load a strong random secret from the environment or a secret manager.
The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded as the weak value '55555'. A predictable secret key enables session cookie forgery. Generate a strong random secret and load it from the environment.
username is concatenated directly into the SQL string passed to cursor.execute("SELECT ... WHERE username = '" + username). This allows SQL injection. Use parameterized queries.
username is interpolated via str.format into the SQL string passed to cursor.execute("... '{}'".format(username)). This allows SQL injection. Use parameterized queries.
username is interpolated via %-formatting into the SQL string passed to cursor.execute("... '%s'" % username). This allows SQL injection. Use parameterized queries.

self.path (user-controlled request path) is concatenated to the filesystem base path (path += self.path) and the resulting path is opened and returned to the client via open(path).read() at line 22. The only filter is a weak regex (line 10) that only blocks a literal '/../..' at the start of the path (re.match), trivially bypassed (e.g. '/foo/../../etc/passwd', URL-encoded %2e%2e, or '....//'). This allows path traversal / arbitrary file read.

The URL is taken from request.args.get('url') (line 13) and fetched server-side via urllib.request.urlopen(url). The only validation is url.startswith('https://insecurewebapp.com') (line 14), which is trivially bypassable (e.g. 'https://insecurewebapp.com@attacker.com' or 'https://insecurewebapp.com.evil.com'), enabling SSRF to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints.

TLS hostname verification is disabled via context.check_hostname = False. This disables certificate hostname validation, allowing man-in-the-middle attacks with a certificate valid for a different hostname. Leave check_hostname True (default) and validate certificates properly.

The payment signature is computed as hashlib.sha256((secret + payment_information).encode()) (data = secret + payment_information at line 17). Using hash(secret || message) as a MAC is vulnerable to hash length-extension attacks, allowing an attacker who observes a valid (message, tag) pair to forge a valid signature for an extended message (e.g. append '&amount=0.00') and tamper with payment data. Use HMAC (hmac.new(secret, msg, hashlib.sha256)).

cwe: CWE-327: Use of a Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm

extra.message: When a 'username' cookie is present (line 13), the server deserializes attacker-controlled cookie data with pickle (Username.pickle() at line 14; the documented sink pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(cookies.get('username').value)) at line 15). Pickle deserialization of untrusted data enables remote code execution via a malicious pickle payload, and no signature/integrity check is present. Use a safe format (e.g. JSON) or cryptographically sign the data.

username (obtained by decrypting the user-supplied session_id cookie at line 26) is written into the HTTP response with bytes("Hello %s" % username) without HTML escaping. Because the IV is read from the attacker-controlled cookie (line 17) and AES-CBC is used without authentication, an attacker can tamper with the cookie (CBC IV bit-flipping) to control the decrypted username and inject script, causing XSS. HTML-encode all output.

AES-CBC decryption (AES.new(KEY, AES.MODE_CBC, iv)) is performed without any MAC/authentication tag, and the IV is taken from the attacker-supplied cookie (line 17). The error path returns HTTP 500 on bad padding while valid padding returns 200, creating a padding oracle that lets an attacker decrypt and forge session cookies, and CBC bit-flipping lets them tamper with plaintext. Use authenticated encryption (AES-GCM or encrypt-then-MAC).

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity
